senses.definition: Direction.
Preparation.
To prepare oneself.
To direct speech.
To aim; to direct.
To prepare or make ready.
To prepare oneself; to apply one's skill or energies (to some object); to betake.
To direct one’s remarks (to someone).
To clothe or array; to dress.
To direct, as words (to anyone or anything); to make, as a speech, petition, etc. (to any audience).
senses.example: He addressed some portions of his remarks to his supporters, some to his opponents.

senses.definition: To direct speech to; to make a communication to, whether spoken or written; to apply to by words, as by a speech, petition, etc., to speak to.
To direct in writing, as a letter; to superscribe, or to direct and transmit.
To confirm or support something with additional evidence; to attest or vouch for.
To make strong; to strengthen.
To make clear; to clarify; to shed light upon.
A force compounded by means of a lever rotating around a pivot; see torque.
senses.example: A crowbar uses leverage to pry nails out of wood.

senses.definition: By extension, any influence which is compounded or used to gain an advantage.
senses.example: Try using competitors’ prices for leverage in the negotiation.

senses.definition: The use of borrowed funds with a contractually determined return to increase the ability of a business to invest and earn an expected higher return, but usually at high risk.
senses.example: Leverage is great until something goes wrong with your investments and you still have to pay your debts.

senses.definition: The ability to earn very high returns when operating at high capacity utilization of a facility.
senses.example: Their variable-cost-reducing investments have dramatically increased their leverage.

senses.definition: To use; to exploit; to manipulate in order to take full advantage (of something).
senses.example: They plan to leverage off the publicity to get a good distribution agreement.

senses.definition: To reduce, lessen, or decrease; to make less severe or easier to bear.
To downplay.
Newly made, formed or evolved; having no precedent; of recent origin; new.
Original, especially in an interesting way; new and striking; not of the typical or ordinary type.
A work of prose fiction, longer than a novella.
A fable; a short tale, especially one of many making up a larger work.
A novelty; something new.
A new legal constitution in ancient Rome.
Evincing strength and health; strong.
senses.example: A robust wall was put up.

senses.definition: Violent; rough; rude.
Requiring strength or vigor
Sensible (of intellect etc.); straightforward, not given to or confused by uncertainty or subtlety
Designed or evolved in such a way as to be resistant to total failure despite partial damage.
Resistant or impervious to failure regardless of user input or unexpected conditions.
Not greatly influenced by errors in assumptions about the distribution of sample errors.
An outwardly projecting part of a fortification, trench system, or line of defense.
Worthy of note; pertinent or relevant.
senses.example: The article is not exhaustive, but it covers the salient points pretty well.

senses.definition: Prominent; conspicuous.
(usually of a quadruped) Depicted in a leaping posture.
Projecting outwards, pointing outwards.
Moving by leaps or springs; jumping.
Shooting or springing out; projecting.
Denoting any angle less than two right angles.
That which has significance; a sign; a token; a symbol.
Signifying something; carrying meaning.
senses.example: a significant word or sound; a significant look

senses.definition: Having a covert or hidden meaning.
Having a noticeable or major effect; notable.
senses.example: That was a significant step in the right direction.

senses.definition: Reasonably large in number or amount.
Having a low probability of occurring by chance (for example, having high correlation and thus likely to be related).
Anything having substance; an essential part.
Having a substance; actually existing.
Not imaginary; real; actual; true; veritable.
Corporeal; material; firm.
Having good substance; strong; stout; solid; firm.
Possessed of goods or an estate; moderately wealthy.
Large in size, quantity, or value; ample; significant.
senses.example: A substantial number of people went to the event.

senses.definition: Most important; essential.
Satisfying; having sufficient substance to be nourishing or filling.
senses.example: I don't just want a snack; I need something substantial.
